# BAD-053 — Split admin/src/lib/actions.ts (1263 lines) into per-domain use server files behind a barrel

## Brief
Plan: [[docs/spikes/bad-036/admin-actions|admin-actions spike]] (Charlotte, BADS-036).

Proposed: admin/src/lib/actions.ts becomes a barrel with no 'use server' directive of its own. Five domain files (accounts, announcements, flags, profiles, collabs) each carry 'use server'; helpers go in two server-only files without it. This layout is a security boundary: an exported async function in a 'use server' file becomes a callable endpoint, so a helper such as deleteAuthUser in one would be an unauthenticated delete. All 34 declarations are placed once. Three files over 250 are argued: flags about 320, accounts about 300, profiles about 270.

Phase 2 touch points: test/server/admin-moderation.test.mjs is re-pointed in the same PR. Related tickets that stay out of this split: [[BAD-050]] (FLAG_VERSION_RE and VERSION_RE copy parseVersion unpinned; moved apart here, never merged) and [[BAD-051]] (the account Edge Function's comments cite actions.ts line numbers; fixed with the next real server change, because editing server/ redeploys).

Verification: the admin's lint, typecheck and build, the export diff and moved-exactly-once scripts, and a signed-in pass through each server action against the local stack per the server-changes skill.

**Gate lifted (Eric, 2026-09-15).** The spike's section 4 layout is approved as written: the barrel plus five 'use server' action leaves and two server-only support leaves, with flags kept whole for the lock order deleteFlag and saveRule share. The layout is unchanged, so the spike needs no edit. Eric also decided the second question the spike left open: the boundary test of section 7 rides with PR 1, so the two support leaves are guarded from their first commit and the moderation test's authorises-before-it-mutates assertion generalises from 6 actions to all 20. It is the one part of PR 1 that is not a pure move, and the PR body says so.

**Rules for Phase 2, from BAD-036.** Split by responsibility; 250 lines is where a file gets a second look, not a cap, and every file left over 250 is argued in the spike's section 6. Every PR is a pure move: no statement is edited, a bug found on the way is its own ticket, and the spike's behaviour-preservation check (section 8) runs on every PR. The public surface in section 2 is the compatibility contract and does not change. Extraction order follows section 9: shared constants, types and pure utilities first, then state and services, then sub-components or handlers, then the entry file reduced to an orchestrator. Verification is the implementing-changes skill's tier for the files touched, quoted in each PR.

## Size, persona and model decision
Phase 2: one engineer on opus per PR in the spike's section 9, in a worktree on a feat/bad-nnn branch after bash scripts/worktree-init.sh; a reviewer at fable tier (opus while the Fable limit holds) checks each PR's pure-move proof before it lands.

## Outcome
Done in two pull requests, both landing on the first merge attempt with every check green. PR 1 (https://github.com/0snug0/BadTakes/pull/370) moved the seven shared declarations into admin/src/lib/actions/support.ts and auth-admin.ts, both server-only and deliberately directive-free, and added test/server/admin-actions-boundary.test.mjs to keep them that way. PR 2 (https://github.com/0snug0/BadTakes/pull/372) moved the twenty actions into five 'use server' leaves and reduced actions.ts to a seventeen-line barrel with no directive of its own. All 34 declarations are placed exactly once across the two: 7 then 27. The twenty exports and their signatures are unchanged, so the six client components were never touched. flags (320), accounts (295) and profiles (265) stay over 250 on the arguments in the spike's section 6.

Two things the plan did not anticipate. The boundary test failed only on the Windows runner, where a CRLF checkout left a carriage return on a line compared for strict equality; the fix routed every line-based rule through one reader without loosening any of them, and was proved by reproducing the failure on a CRLF tree first. And the spike's section 8 step 4 glob predates PR 1, so run literally after it lands the check reports PR 1's helpers as CODE ADDED — the scoped run is each PR's real accounting. Both facts are recorded in the pull requests.

The boundary test needed no edit in PR 2, which is the outcome worth keeping: the guard written alongside the first move held across the second without being adjusted to fit it.
